description: A Chinese-style braise of soy, orange, and five-spice — savory and warm, not too sweet or spicy. Nothing here is time-critical, so it's an easy one to cook together; the prep and braise can be done ahead, and the ribs reheat beautifully.

ingredients.raw: 5 pounds (2.25 kg) beef short ribs (see note)

ingredients.item: kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.raw: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
2 tablespoons (30 ml) neutral oil, such as vegetable or canola
3 tablespoons peeled and grated fresh ginger (from about one 3-inch knob)

ingredients.prep: for zest — one in wide strips, one finely grated
ingredients.raw: Zest of 2 oranges, one in wide strips, one finely grated, divided
1/2 cup (120 ml) fresh juice from about 2 medium oranges, divided
1/2 cup (120 ml) Shaoxing rice wine (or dry sherry)
1/4 cup (60 ml) unseasoned rice wine vinegar
2 tablespoons (30 ml) sambal chili paste or Chinese chili-garlic sauce

ingredients.note: or water, plus more as needed
ingredients.raw: 3 1/2 cups (830 ml) homemade or store-bought low-sodium chicken stock or water, plus more as needed

ingredients.note: whisked with an equal amount of cold water into a slurry
ingredients.raw: 1 1/2 tablespoons (18 g) cornstarch mixed with 1 1/2 tablespoons (20 ml) cold water

ingredients.prep: white and light green parts only, thinly sliced
ingredients.raw: 3 scallions, white and light green parts only, thinly sliced, for garnish

notes: Buy the English cut of short ribs — one large bone per piece. Avoid flanken-cut (thin, cross-cut, several bones per piece).
Make-ahead: nothing is time-critical and the ribs reheat well, so you can brown and braise ahead, then finish the sauce later.
Leftovers: pull the meat off the bones, shred it, toss with the sauce, and fold into tacos with cabbage and pickled onions.

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350°F (180°C) — or plug in a slow cooker.

brief: Pat the ribs dry; season lightly with salt, generously with pepper.
Heat the oil in a Dutch oven over medium-high until shimmering.
Sear the ribs in a single layer, in batches, browning well on all sides; move to a plate.
Pour off all but about 2 tbsp of the fat.
steps.text: Pat the short ribs dry. Season both sides lightly with salt and more generously with black pepper. Heat the oil in a Dutch oven over medium-high heat until shimmering, then add the ribs in a single layer — work in batches so you sear rather than steam them. Brown well on all sides, transfer to a plate, and pour off all but about 2 tablespoons of the fat.
Add the onion, ginger, garlic, and five-spice powder. Cook over medium-high heat, stirring, until the onions soften and everything is fragrant, about 4 minutes.

brief: Add the orange zest strips and {{0.25 cup}} orange juice, plus the Shaoxing wine, soy sauce, rice vinegar, honey, chili paste, hoisin, and stock; stir.
Return the ribs and any juices to the pot (or move everything to a slow cooker).
steps.text: Add the wide strips of orange zest and {{0.25 cup}} of the orange juice, along with the Shaoxing wine, soy sauce, rice vinegar, honey, chili paste, hoisin, and stock. Stir to combine, then return the ribs and any accumulated juices to the pot. (Or transfer everything to a slow cooker.)
Slow cooker: cover and cook on high until the meat is tender and frees easily from the bones, 6 to 8 hours.

Dutch oven: bring to a boil, cover, and transfer to the oven. Braise until the ribs are tender, about 3 hours, checking now and then and adding stock or water if it looks dry. Take the lid off for the last 20 minutes. The meat should be very tender but not completely falling apart.

brief: Lift out the ribs and keep warm. Strain the liquid, spoon off the fat, and return the sauce to the pot; discard the solids.
Stir in the remaining {{0.25 cup}} orange juice; you want about {{3 cup}} of sauce — simmer to reduce if you have more.
Whisk in just enough cornstarch slurry to lightly thicken, a tablespoon at a time.
steps.text: Lift out the ribs and keep them warm. Strain the braising liquid, then separate or spoon off the fat and return the defatted sauce to the pot; discard the solids. Stir in the remaining {{0.25 cup}} orange juice. You want about {{3 cup}} of sauce — if you have more, simmer to reduce. Whisk in just enough of the cornstarch slurry to lightly thicken it, a tablespoon at a time; you may not need it all.
Return the ribs to the sauce and coat them well. Scatter with the sliced scallions and the finely grated orange zest, and serve over mashed potatoes or polenta.

subtitle: Tender, saucy short ribs with warm five-spice and a bright citrus lift
title: Braised Chinese-Style Short Ribs with Soy, Orange, and Five-Spice
